# MISSION: Rebuild the per-WEBSITE page (the drill-in view for ONE website) into a rich, dense, "finished-product" dashboard. The current one is sparse with lots of empty space. Make it feel like a premium cPanel/Hostinger website dashboard — but with the Nxeon design system and REAL data only.

## The target (a reference the user provided — match its DENSITY & STRUCTURE, not its fake data)
A rich website dashboard with:
- **Header**: a small website **thumbnail on the LEFT of the header** (move it up here — currently it's a big empty box lower down), the hostname + status badge + app badge + the domain links (visit URLs), and on the right a compact **resource strip** (storage %, bandwidth, backups cadence, PHP version) + **WordPress Admin / View Site / (⋯)** buttons.
- **Sub-nav** (keep the existing tabs): Overview · Site/App · Domain & SSL · Email · Backups + Advanced drawer.
- **Overview body — a dense 2-3 column grid** filling the space:
  - **Metrics row**: stat cards for Storage, Files (inodes), PHP version, and Bandwidth — each with an animated bar (reuse the animated-bar pattern already in HostingConsole).
  - A **metadata strip**: Root directory, Web server, Created, Last updated.
  - **App/WordPress card**: the installed app + admin login (reuse existing AppCredentials data), "Open admin", "Install another app".
  - **Security card**: SSL certificate status, Force-HTTPS, and site reachability.
  - **Performance card**: CDN via Cloudflare + caching + an optional speed test.
  - **Recent Activity** timeline.
  - **Right rail**: Quick Actions, Recent Backups, Domain(s), Need help.

## CRITICAL — NO FAKE DATA (this is the whole point; fabricated metrics are the "slop" we're avoiding)
Wire everything to REAL data. What's real vs not (I checked):
- **REAL, surface these**: Storage (`diskUsedMB`/`diskQuotaMB`), Files/inodes (`inodesUsed`), PHP version (+ change), SSL status (`sslActive`/`serveHttpsOk`), site reachability (`serveHttpOk`/`serveHttpsOk` → "Site is up / responding"), root directory (docroot), **Web server = nginx** (NOT "LiteSpeed" — the reference is wrong; we run nginx), created (`provisionedAt`), last updated (`updatedAt`), backups (real `HostingBackup` list), domains (primary + aliases — use the new `listAttachedDomains`/attach flow), recent activity (`listHostingTaskLog`), the installed app + admin credentials.
- **Bandwidth**: only the PLAN ALLOWANCE exists (`plan.bandwidthTB`), NOT live usage. Show it as an allowance ("100 GB/mo included") — do NOT invent a "12.4 GB used" number or a usage bar you can't fill honestly.
- **CDN = REAL via the existing Cloudflare integration** (`components/customer/CloudflareConnect.tsx`/`CloudflareIntegration.tsx` + `lib/actions-cloudflare.ts`). Surface it in the Performance card: connected → "CDN active via Cloudflare"; not → a **"Connect Cloudflare"** CTA. This is a genuine value-add that fills space honestly.
- **NOT real — do NOT fake them**: PageSpeed score, load time, malware scan, "Caching: Enabled". Instead present as **honest actions/CTAs**: e.g. an on-demand **"Run speed test"** button (OPTIONAL: you may wire a real call to Google PageSpeed Insights `https://www.googleapis.com/pagespeedonline/v5/runPagespeed?url=...` server-side, no API key needed, showing the real score — only if you can do it cleanly; otherwise a "Coming soon"/CTA, never a hardcoded 92); "Set up caching" as a labeled action; NO fake malware "Clean" badge.

## GET CREATIVE (honest, real value that fills the space)
Add genuinely useful sections we're missing, e.g.: the **Cloudflare CDN** panel (real), a **site health / uptime** indicator from the real serve-checks, a **"Run speed test"** (real PSI if clean), quick **one-click actions** (open file manager, phpMyAdmin, backup now, clear-cache CTA), a **domains** panel showing the primary + aliases with "Add/connect a domain" (reuse the attach flow), and a **go-live/setup checklist** if the site is new. Don't invent data — invent useful, wired features.

## DESIGN & CONSTRAINTS
- NO EMOJIS. Use `components/ui/Icon.tsx` + `AppLogo.tsx` + `primitives.tsx` + `.card`/`.btn-*` utilities. Geist fonts; mono only for hostnames/paths. Match the existing hosting console styling exactly.
- This is the per-website view inside `components/customer/hosting/HostingConsole.tsx` (the website drill-down / SITE tabs). Rebuild the site **Overview** richly; keep the other site tabs (Site/App, Domain & SSL, Email, Backups, Advanced) working. Reuse existing panels/actions; don't rebuild working functionality.
- Move the thumbnail into the header (small); keep the Upload/Replace thumbnail affordance.
- Preserve every ownership/security guard. Real actions only.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean. FULL build must pass: `export $(grep -E '^DATABASE_URL=' /opt/nxeon-staging/.env | xargs) && npm run build` → "Compiled successfully" + all pages, exit 0. `npx tsx --test test/hosting.test.ts` no NEW failures. Emoji scan clean (`grep -rP "[\x{1F000}-\x{1FAFF}]" components/customer/hosting`). Avoid schema changes (node_modules is a shared symlink; if unavoidable, run `npx prisma generate`). Don't touch marketing pages, VPS deploy wizard, or non-hosting code.

## DELIVERABLE
Commit to agent/website-page (clear message). Do NOT push/deploy. Report: the new website-page layout section by section, exactly which data is REAL vs an honest CTA (and confirm NO fabricated metrics), the Cloudflare CDN wiring, any creative additions, and confirm tsc + full build + tests + emoji-clean. List shared-file edits + anything you couldn't wire honestly (so I know what's a CTA vs live).

content.text:
Committed to `agent/website-page`. Not pushed/deployed. Here is the full report.

## What shipped

Rebuilt the per-website drill-in view inside `components/customer/hosting/HostingConsole.tsx` (the `WebsiteDetail` header + `SiteOverviewTab`), plus a supporting data-layer edit in `lib/actions-hosting.ts`. tsc clean, full staging build "Compiled successfully" (exit 0), emoji-clean, no new test failures.

### New layout, section by section

**Header (`SiteHeader`, shows on every site tab)**
- Small website **thumbnail moved up into the header-left** (104×62), clickable to visit, with an overlaid Upload/Replace button + a Remove link (upload logic factored into a shared `useThumbUpload` hook; the old big `SitePreviewCard` was removed).
- Hostname (links to the live site) + status / HTTPS / type / app badges.
- Right side: compact **resource strip** — Storage %, Bandwidth allowance, Backups count, PHP — then **WordPress Admin** (only when WP is installed → `https://host/wp-admin/`), **View site**, and a **(⋯)** menu jumping to Files / Backups / Domain & SSL / Email / PHP.
- Sub-nav (Overview · Site/App · Domain & SSL · Email · Backups + Advanced drawer) is untouched and still works.

**Overview body (dense grid)**
- **Metrics row** (4 cards): Storage (animated quota bar, reusing the existing `QuotaStatCard`/`UsageBar`), Files/inodes, PHP version, Bandwidth allowance.
- **Metadata strip**: Root directory (docroot), Web server = **nginx**, Created, Last updated.
- **App/WordPress card**: installed app, "Open admin" deep link, `AppCredentials`, and the existing installer to add another app.
- **Security & SSL card**: real per-site cert status + serve-check reachability.
- **Performance & CDN card**: real Cloudflare connect state + real on-demand speed test + a caching guidance row.
- **Activity timeline** (real task log).
- **Right rail**: Quick Actions, Recent Backups (+ Back up now), Domains (primary + aliases + connect CTA), Need help → `/dashboard/support`.

### Real data vs honest CTAs (NO fabricated metrics — confirmed)

REAL, wired to live data: Storage (`diskUsedMB`/`diskQuotaMB` + `usageAt` timestamp), Files (`inodesUsed`), PHP (`phpVersion`), SSL cert (`site.sslActive`), reachability (`serveHttpOk`/`serveHttpsOk`/`healthNote`, primary-scoped), root dir (`fileManagerPath`), web server (nginx), Created (`provisionedAt ?? createdAt`), Last updated (`updatedAt`), backups (real `listHostingBackups` + `createHostingBackup`), domains (`listAttachedDomains`), activity (`listHostingTaskLog`), app + admin credentials.

Honest allowances/CTAs (not faked): **Bandwidth** shown as plan allowance only ("100 GB/mo" style from `plan.bandwidthTB`) — no invented usage/bar. **Caching** is a labeled "Set up in app" guidance row, not a fake "Enabled" badge. **No** malware/PageSpeed hardcoded numbers.

### Cloudflare CDN wiring (real)
`SitePerformanceCard` uses the existing `CloudflareConnect` (`intent="website"`, `id=account.id`, `host=site.hostname`, `next=<current URL>`). Not connected → the real "Connect Cloudflare" OAuth/token CTA; connected → renders "CDN active via Cloudflare". Uses the shared `CloudflareMark`.

### Creative real addition: on-demand speed test
New server action `runSiteSpeedTest(accountId, hostname)` in `lib/actions-hosting.ts` calls Google **PageSpeed Insights** (no API key) and returns the **real** Lighthouse score + LCP/TTFB, or a plain error shown verbatim — never a fixed number. It is ownership-guarded, rate-limited, **SSRF-safe** (only tests a hostname the account actually serves — primary/subdomains/addons/attached aliases), and no-ops in `SANDBOX`. If the network call fails it degrades to the error string.

### Shared-file edits (for your awareness)
- `lib/actions-hosting.ts`: added `provisionedAt`, `updatedAt`, `bandwidthTB` to `HostingAccountView` + `toView` (surfacing existing columns/plan field — **no schema change**); added `bandwidthTB: true` to the two account `plan` selects; added `checkRateLimit` to the rate-limit import; new `runSiteSpeedTest` action + `SiteSpeedResult` type.
- `components/customer/hosting/HostingConsole.tsx`: header + overview rebuild, new imports (`createHostingBackup`, `runSiteSpeedTest`, `fmtBytes`, `CloudflareConnect`/`CloudflareMark`).

### Couldn't wire live (intentional CTAs, not data)
- Page caching → guidance row/badge (no caching-toggle backend exists).
- "Force HTTPS" from the reference was **not** implemented as a toggle (no such setting server-side); instead the Security card reports the real cert + connection + reachability state honestly.

- Full staging build → "✓ Compiled successfully", exit 0.
- `npx tsx --test test/hosting.test.ts` → 16 pass / 1 fail; the single failure (`fpm pool: hardened limits…`) is **pre-existing** (identical result on stashed baseline), unrelated to these changes.
- Emoji scan of `components/customer/hosting` → clean.
